stories.title: More Than 14,000 Derelict Explosives Cleared from Libyan City and Nearby Farmland
stories.label: peace
stories.summary: A coastal city in Libya and the farmland around it are a lot safer this year, thanks to a careful team effort. The United Nations' mission in Libya, Italian aid workers, local Libyan partners, and the demining group HALO Trust worked together to clear more than 14,000 old landmines and unexploded bombs left over from past conflict. That means farmers can till their fields without fear, and families can walk their own streets without worrying about what's buried beneath them. It's slow, careful work, but it's already done and it's already making daily life safer for real people.
stories.why_good: A real, completed humanitarian achievement that directly removes danger from people's homes and farmland, with no political framing.

stories.title: How NYC Students Saved School Lunch
stories.label: people
stories.summary: A group of New York City students decided they were tired of skipping the cafeteria because the food was bad and eating there felt embarrassing. Instead of just complaining, they worked with their school to redesign the lunch program itself, improving the food and the whole experience of eating together. More students are now actually showing up to eat real meals instead of avoiding the cafeteria. It's a simple, human win: kids got a say in something that affects them every single day, and it worked.
stories.why_good: A real, already-implemented improvement to kids' daily nutrition and school life, driven by the students themselves, with no political fight involved.
